title: Period and Phase-Shifted Graph of y = sin(x + pi/6)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the fundamental period of y = \sin(x + \pi/6) and describe its horizontal shift and key points over one cycle.

steps.title: Determine the Fundamental Period
steps.explanation: Because the multiplier of x is 1, the period of y = sin(x + pi/6) is 2*pi.
steps.why: Adding a constant phase angle inside the argument shifts the wave without stretching or compressing it.

steps.title: Identify the Horizontal Phase Shift
steps.explanation: Writing x + pi/6 as x - (-pi/6) shows that the standard sine curve is shifted pi/6 units to the left.
steps.why: Replacing x by x + c with c > 0 translates a graph horizontally to the left by c units.

steps.title: Locate Key Quarter-Period Points on [-pi/6, 11*pi/6]
steps.explanation: Subtracting pi/6 from each standard sine landmark 0, pi/2, pi, 3*pi/2, 2*pi gives the exact coordinates for one full cycle.
steps.why: Every feature of y = sin x shifts left by pi/6 while preserving its y-value.
